subject: Post-call: Hosted latency qualification and PoC proposal for Nimble Health
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@nimblehealth.com>, Tom Gibson <tom.gibson@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Hosted latency qualification and PoC proposal for Nimble Health

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful conversation and good signal on what matters for your inference surface. Short recap and proposed next steps below so we all have the same plan.

Call highlights (quick):
- Primary SLOs you care about: end-to-end p95 and p99 for the user-facing generation endpoint.
- Current provider baseline you shared: p95 ~240ms, p99 ~700ms (at your peak traffic patterns).
- Target you’d like to evaluate on a hosted provider: p95 in the ~100–160ms window and p99 ideally under ~400ms.
- Throughput and concurrency: typical sustained 120 rps with short bursts to 350 rps; streaming sessions for live-assist feature ~40–60 concurrent streams during peak.
- Important: consistent tail behavior for longer prompts (~1.5–2k tokens) and streaming chunk latency for interactive UX.

Proposed PoC plan (summary):
1) Redwood-run benchmark (dry run): we will run a synthetic and replay test using a 24-hour sample you provide. Goal: measure e2e p95/p99 hosted vs your baseline.
2) Live PoC week (1 week): ingress via a dedicated hosted endpoint with realistic concurrency. We’ll instrument per-token and end-to-end tracing and give daily dashboards.
3) Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 150ms and p99 <= 350ms for your nominal request mix OR documented tradeoffs and mitigation (e.g., model variant, quantization, request shaping).

Action items (owners):
- Asha/Tom (Nimble): share a 24-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized), typical request sizes, and a list of 3 representative prompts by EOD 6/14. Attachment stub: nimble_latency_sample.csv.
- Ben (Redwood): draft test config and baseline scripts; propose traffic shaping and streaming concurrency settings by EOD 6/14.
- Marissa (Redwood): prepare pricing/POC cost estimate and an enterprise data flow diagram for your security team.
- Sergio (me): coordinate test dates, provide the hosted endpoint, and own daily status updates.

I’ll follow up with the detailed PoC plan and the Redwood-side test harness (link to Drive) once Ben confirms the config. If this sounds right to you, please reply with the sample file and preferred start date for the live week.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: nimble_latency_sample.csv (csv) — small telemetry sample you mentioned on the call.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha@nimblehealth.com>, Tom Gibson <tom.gibson@nimblehealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosted latency qualification and PoC proposal for Nimble Health

Nice recap. A couple of clarifying questions from the runtime perspective before I lock configs: 

1) Token distribution: do you have the 50/90/99 token length percentiles? We need the tail distribution to size KV cache and attention kernels. If not, the sample CSV is fine.
2) Streaming behavior: when you say "streaming chunk latency," do you mean server->client chunk emit interval (we aim for <=50ms for smooth typing) or is it the round-trip for interactive edits? Both matter but we’ll tune the former in the runtime.
3) Concurrency shape: is the 350 rps burst sustained for longer than 30s or is it a sub-10s spike? That changes how we size burst capacity.

Proposed Redwood test config (initial):
- Model variant: 8-bit quantized v1.3 (fallback to fp16 v1.3 for quality-sensitive paths).
- Batch window: adaptive up to 12ms with priority skew for streaming sessions.
- Target concurrency for PoC: sustained 120 rps, burst to 350 rps for 60s.
- Streaming sessions: 60 concurrent streams, chunk emit target 45ms.

I’ll put together the exact load spec and a reproducible gatling-style profile and share the test harness link. If Asha can drop the sample and a short list of the most critical prompts, we’ll map those to the test mix.

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: redwood_poc_plan.pdf (draft)

From: Asha Patel <asha@nimblehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Gibson <tom.gibson@nimblehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosted latency qualification and PoC proposal for Nimble Health

Thanks — this matches our notes. Quick answers inline: 

- Token distribution: attaching a small CSV snippet (nimble_latency_sample.csv). 50/90/99 token sizes are ~43/220/1,720 respectively (we see long tails from conversation history).
- Streaming chunk: we mean server->client chunk emit. Our UX team expects <=50ms per chunk for live typing to feel real-time; end-to-end p95 for first token is critical.
- Burst shape: burst events typically last 20–90s (depends on campaign windows). We can simulate 60s bursts for the PoC.

Acceptable PoC start: 2027-06-21 (week of). We’re happy to do the dry run the prior week if Redwood wants to validate setup.

One thing to flag: our security/compliance team will want a short architecture diagram and confirmation that telemetry traces do not include PII. Marissa, if you can share the data flow diagram and a short note about telemetry redaction, that would help speed our internal approval.

Tom is the engineering champion here — he’ll coordinate on the sample and schedule.

Best,
Asha Patel
Head of Platform | Nimble Health
asha@nimblehealth.com

Attachment: nimble_latency_sample.csv (anonymized)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosted latency qualification and PoC proposal for Nimble Health

Perfect — thanks for the sample and the timeline confirmation. Quick update on next steps from Redwood side: 

1) Dry run (internal): Ben and I will run the initial synthetic against your sample on 6/17 to validate the harness. No customer traffic will be routed yet; results posted to the Drive folder and Datadog link.
2) Live PoC week: provisioned hosted endpoint for 6/21–6/28. We’ll instrument: per-token timing, prefix cache hit rates, and a p95/p99 breakdown by request size bucket.
3) Acceptance criteria tweak: given your token tail, we’ll use conditional acceptance: 
   - For requests <= 500 tokens: p95 <= 125ms, p99 <= 300ms.
   - For requests > 500 tokens: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 420ms, with mitigation notes if we need to recommend request shaping or a different model variant.

Marissa will send the enterprise diagram and telemetry redaction note (cc’d). Ben will share the exact load spec and the Gatling profile by 6/15 so your team can sanity-check.

Can you confirm Tom as the PoC engineering point-of-contact and the desired daily sync time (we propose 9:30am PT)?

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
